_source: ServUO. Every BaseDoor subclass is base(closed + 2 * facing, closed + 1 + 2 * facing, ...), so a family is `count` consecutive graphics with the shut leaves on the even offsets and the open ones on the odd. Scripts/Items/Functional/Doors.cs holds the thirteen plain ones, SecretDoors.cs six more, and SlidingDoors.cs three that use only four of the eight facings and are therefore eight graphics wide rather than sixteen.
_why: Nothing in the client's own files says which of a door's graphics is the open one. tiledata.mul gives an open leaf the stopping flags of its shut twin - measured, identical in 103 of the 104 plain pairs; the DOOR flag comes in runs of 1 to 98 graphics so there is no parity to read off the layout; and 'an open leaf's picture is wider than a tile' holds for 46 of those pairs because a door swung to four of the eight facings is still 44 across. See docs/lighting.md, decision 11.
_not_here: Portcullis.cs is deliberately absent: PortcullisNS and PortcullisEW are base(0x6F5, 0x6F5) and base(0x6F6, 0x6F6) - one graphic for both states, because a portcullis is raised in z rather than swung. There is nothing to tell apart, and a table cannot invent it.
